proposed_definition_changes.reason: The full-rectangle replacement for an empty raw Hall region is an off-coverage totalization with nonzero length. At boundary parameters such as \(\alpha_{xa}=4\), the two threshold count errors have a nondegenerate limiting distribution, so the fixed-level Clopper--Pearson strips can imply only indices above four with a positive limiting probability; the raw region is then empty. On that event the full rectangle makes the maximal width order \(\ell\), defeating the asserted \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) width even though coverage may fail there. Replacing an empty raw region and an empty final intersection by singletons changes output only off the joint count-coverage event, preserves the exact coverage proof, and gives zero rather than global fallback length.

proposed.name: \(\Theta_{xa}\)
proposed.def: Let \(\Theta^\circ_{xa}\) be the set of \((\alpha,v)\in[1,4]\times[-\log2,0]\) satisfying \(\log\underline S_{xa}(z)-\log(1+Dz^{-\beta})\le v-\alpha\log z\le\log\overline S_{xa}(z)-\log(1-Dz^{-\beta})\) at both \(z=T^{\mathrm{ci}}_{n,m}\) and \(z=eT^{\mathrm{ci}}_{n,m}\), with \(\log0=-\infty\). Set \(\Theta_{xa}=\Theta^\circ_{xa}\) when the raw region is nonempty, and set \(\Theta_{xa}=\{(1,-\log2)\}\) otherwise.
proposed.role: bias-aware parameter region with zero-width off-coverage totalization

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the symbol catalog with the corrected empty-region totalization; the former full rectangle can force a nonshrinking width on a fixed positive-probability off-coverage event.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(I_{\pi}\)

proposed.name: \(I_{\pi}\)
proposed.type: confidence interval for a log policy value
proposed.def: On \(N<b_{\beta,D}\log(40m)\), set \(I_{\pi}=G_{\tau}\). Otherwise put \(J^*_{\pi}=[\underline t_{\pi}-\varepsilon_{\tau},\overline t_{\pi}+\varepsilon_{\tau}]\). If \(J^*_{\pi}\cap G_{\tau}\) is nonempty, set \(I_{\pi}=J^*_{\pi}\cap G_{\tau}\); otherwise set \(I_{\pi}\) to the singleton containing the metric projection of the midpoint of \(J^*_{\pi}\) onto \(G_{\tau}\).
proposed.role: inference output with zero-width off-coverage totalization

proposed_core_edits.reason: Keep the interval symbol total and length-controlled when its bias-expanded core interval misses the global Hall interval off the simultaneous coverage event.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine the distribution, under the product paired-splice prior and an unrestricted capacity-constrained learner, of the number \(H\) of missed heavy cells at testing information from order one through order \(\log m\), and match the resulting exact expected log-sum-exp loss by a full-class learner without coordinatewise familywise localization.
open_obligations.obstruction: Assouad's argument proves only \(\mathbb E H\gtrsim m\) at constant neighboring information. For larger information, the loss is concave and nonlinear in \(H\), so neither a mean Hamming-error lower bound nor Jensen's inequality supplies the required lower bound. Capacity reallocation can correlate errors across pairs, while a coordinatewise upper proof pays \((\log m)^{\varkappa}\). The frozen primitives contain no distributional ambiguity lemma closing this gap.
open_obligations.attempted: I derived the exact missed-cell regret equation, checked same-class Hall membership and neighboring product divergence, expanded the fixed-information Assouad bound, and proved the coordinatewise thresholded upper bound. I also tested the sparse-error route against the capacity projection inequality; it controls the mean at constant information but does not control the rare-event law needed when \(\delta\ell\) is large.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove a matching confidence-length lower bound over all total simultaneous systems and derive the necessary-and-sufficient joint-sequence condition for a shrinking maximal width, separately from policy regret.
open_obligations.obstruction: The paired family supplies bounded neighboring divergence, but confidence-set testing duality must retain the \(m^{-1}\)-weighted mixture separation for a growing collection of policies. A one-coordinate two-point argument is diluted by \(1/m\), whereas an Assouad mean-separation argument does not by itself lower-bound the maximum simultaneous interval length. No frozen result bridges that distinction. In addition, the current upper-system definition requires the emitted empty-region correction before its stochastic width claim is true.
open_obligations.attempted: I verified exact Bonferroni coverage from the \(4m\) binomial inversions, propagated Hall strips to core roots, and analyzed the paired-splice neighboring divergence. I also checked the empty-region fallback at boundary indices and found that its positive-probability global width invalidates the present shrinking-in-probability claim, motivating the definition correction in this bundle.
